paper.title: Multiple myeloma: retrospective assessment of routine thromboprophylaxis and utility of thrombotic risk scores.

source.title: Multiple myeloma: retrospective assessment of routine thromboprophylaxis and utility of thrombotic risk scores.

study.setting: Instituto Nacional de Cancerologia, Mexico City, Mexico, tertiary referral cancer center
study.multivariateScoreItemAnalysis: Reported only in unchecked supplementary table, not verified here

results.outcome: Observed VTE burden under routine mostly aspirin primary prophylaxis
Major and clinically relevant nonmajor bleeding with overlap and concomitant treatment limits
Risk score discrimination and group rates with unresolved PRISM denominator/test labels
Survival by ever-VTE status is inconclusive rather than proof of no mortality impact

claims.statement: Among250selectedretrospectivepatients,37labeledVTEoccurredduringvariablefollowup,including20within6months,underpredominantlyASA81mgprophylaxis. The source endpoint includes superficial/temporal-vein events. No suitable comparative control establishes causal aspirin inefficacy/harm or DOAC superiority.

Risk-score discrimination was imprecise,allFigure2AUC CIsincluding50%. IMPEDEROC P.09 differsfromgroup-rate/logranktests;PRISMNs167versusTable156remainunresolved. These results do not establish universal tool invalidity or a clinically effective prescribing rule.

sourceQualifications.description: Retrospective single-center cohort, almost all prescribed aspirin, no suitable randomized or balanced alternative-agent/no-prophylaxis comparison. Residual VTE/bleeding burden does not isolate causal aspirin inefficacy/harm, DOAC superiority or a new prescription. Authors unacceptable-risk/change-strategy wording is attributed interpretation, not adopted judgment.

Tertiary referral population, mostly intermediate/highrisk with high-dose steroids/thalidomide, not general low-risk or modern lenalidomide cohorts.
